proposed_fix.description: Locate where the inbound-call delay is introduced (network path, sidecar, or node-level contention) and apply a gated, reversible mitigation such as rescheduling or restarting the affected pod only after a human approves.
steps: Compare productcatalogservice inbound span durations by caller and by pod/node to see whether the ~200ms delay is uniform or concentrated on one pod, node, or caller (E2).
Check for a recent change (deploy, config, mesh/network policy, injected fault) affecting productcatalogservice around the onset of the latency jump (E1, E3).
Inspect node-level network health (receive errors, drops, conntrack usage) on the nodes hosting productcatalogservice pods; only act on R2/R3 if those metrics are actually abnormal.
If a single pod or node is the outlier, cordon that node or delete that pod so it reschedules (human-approved); one replica at a time.
If a recent change is identified, roll it back through the normal deploy process after approval.
Watch productcatalogservice latency-50/90 and recommendationservice latency (E1) for recovery after each action.
preconditions: Confirm the latency deviation is still ongoing and not already recovered.
Confirm other healthy replicas exist so removing one pod does not reduce capacity (workload is already down 23.4%, E3).
Obtain on-call approval before any cordon, pod deletion, or rollback.
Record current pod/node placement and config version so the state can be restored.
proposed_fix.rollback: Uncordon any cordoned node, let the scheduler restore pod placement (or redeploy the previous replica count), and re-apply the prior config/deploy version if a rollback was performed; each step is individually reversible.
